findings.where: s2load.py:509-520 (pair_problem), called for every load at s2load.py:641; the claim is stated at s2load.py:24-26 and in LOADER_RULE (s2load.py:109-116), which import_tar copies into the validation record
findings.problem: A judging (inference) load unpickles the VecNormalize .pkl. Rule K9 and design D14 say a load for judging lets only tensors and the policy class cross library versions, and that the .pkl is read only by a training resume. pair_problem calls the repository's checkpoint_pair_problem, which runs pickle.load on the sidecar (environments/shared/curriculum/checkpoints.py:203-204). So two gymnasium Box spaces, a numpy Generator with its PCG64 and SeedSequence state, RunningMeanStd and VecNormalize are unpickled on every check, import, monitor and row load. A sidecar that does not unpickle under this machine's libraries makes the checkpoint 'not judged' even though the judged path does not need it. The builder followed the brief (it asks for checkpoint_pair_problem in every load), so the brief and K9 disagree; s2load.py enters the rows' sources at state B, so this must be settled before the freeze.
findings.evidence: Scratch run exp_misc.py (log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/2dca1c00-13f3-5853-acf6-8c3e3e04feb6/scratchpad/review_wpc_cp/logs/exp_misc.log). findings.where: s2load.py:600-604 (_read_fingerprint catches OSError, ValueError, KeyError only)

findings.where: s2load.py:338-342 (fingerprint uses model.predict, which clips to the action bounds) and s2load.py:448-450 (the record's fingerprint block)
findings.problem: Suggestion beyond the brief, for the lead to accept or drop before s2load.py is frozen at state B. The record says how many rows the normalisation clips but not how many fingerprint actions sit on the action bounds. predict clips actions to +-1 (stable_baselines3/common/policies.py:379), and a column with almost no variance in training sends every fingerprint row to the +-10 clip. An entry on a bound cannot show a difference, so a fingerprint with many such entries proves less than its 4,352 numbers suggest, and nothing in the record tells a reader.
findings.evidence: A constructed illustration, not a measurement on a trained policy: the scratch checkpoint with the four head_command columns given zero variance and the output layer scaled by 300 has all 256 rows clipped by the normalisation and 2,857 of 4,352 action entries (66 %) exactly on a bound; one output weight += 0.01 then changes 76 of 256 entries of that action. On the fresh stub policy no entry is on a bound (max |action| 0.026).
findings.fix: Add to the record's fingerprint block at s2load.py:448-450: "actions_at_bound": int(np.count_nonzero(np.abs(actions) >= 1.0)), with one assertion in test_the_record_and_the_four_files; the monitor or the report can then flag a checkpoint whose fingerprint is mostly saturated.

verdict: No blocker; two major findings to settle before s2load.py is frozen at state B, and the rest is minor. The code does what S2-12, S2-13, S2-14 and rules K2, K4, K9 ask, with one exception: a judging load unpickles the VecNormalize .pkl through the repository's integrity check, which K9 and D14 say it does not (the brief asked for that check on every load, so the lead must rule). The second major is a test gap: removing the normalisation from the fingerprint passes all 35 loader tests. What I verified myself, on the branch head 8aa5ce3 with the worktree left untouched: the 54 tests pass (18 s) and the acceptance commands check, pack and import exit 0 with "fingerprint 0.0" and identical tar bytes twice. An archive saved with the schedule classes, and one saved by a resumed session, hold no bytecode in any pickle stream (the data members and the three torch archives, walked with pickletools); the committed Stage 1 checkpoint 75-M-H-10/ppo/42 holds cloudpickled closures in learning_rate and lr_schedule. A missing, truncated or mismatched file is refused in every case tried, with one edge that raises BadZipFile instead of CheckpointError. The fingerprint reproduces with difference 0.0 in a fresh process and with 1, 2 and 4 torch threads. It fails for perturbed statistics and for a perturbed weight whose effect on an action exceeds 1e-5 (one output weight += 1e-4 is refused). On the freshly initialised stub policy one first-layer weight += 0.01 moves the actions by 8.3e-6 and loads, and critic weights and log_std are invisible to it; both follow from the rule's absolute tolerance on deterministic actions, not from the code. Torch's build label is dropped on both sides of every comparison. The CLI assigns MUJOCO_GL before mujoco is imported whether it starts under osmesa, egl or unset, and no GL library is mapped; only the test file's script entry does not assign it. A child started under osmesa that calls assign_gl first builds and trains a policy with exit 0; the control without the assignment did not segfault here either, even with a live OSMesa context, so on this container the "no segfault" check cannot discriminate. Only the six owned files changed after the clean merge of wt/wp-r; nothing under designlab/stage1 and no round-A module differs; commit messages end with the two required lines; no test or log runs an episode on any Stage 2 set (stub env only). Every one of the 53 test functions was made to fail by at least one scratch mutation; the surviving mutations are the test gaps listed. Evidence and scripts are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/2dca1c00-13f3-5853-acf6-8c3e3e04feb6/scratchpad/review_wpc_cp/ (logs/ holds every run).
